blindSummary:
This state/province holds a dedicated integral law on the right to gender identity and expression, alongside a general LGBT-protection statute, making it one of only two state/provinces in the country to have enacted legislation in both the trans-specific and the general-LGBT-equality categories. Unlike the state/province that contains the national capital, this one has not amended or narrowed its provisions. The statutory framework supports institutional response channels for a visitor encountering discrimination.

No incident data, enforcement action, or negative visitor-facing finding was located for this state/province in the research pass. Its largest city has a visible and well-established LGBTQ community with dedicated infrastructure. The divergence from the national average is modest and rests on the statutory-completeness evidence.

The position is marginally above the national average, reflecting a dual-category legislative framework (gender identity plus LGBT equality) that is active and unrevised. The state/province containing the national capital shares the dual-category structure but actively rolled back its provisions in 2023, so this state/province is clearly safer than it. Another state/province has no such law at all; the gap there is driven entirely by the presence versus absence of statutory infrastructure.
